newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese PM states 'remorse' for Asian war victims.
newsitem.headline: Japanese PM states 'remorse' for Asian war victims.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto marked the 52nd anniversary of the end of World War Two on Friday by saying he felt "deep remorse" for Asian victims of Japanese militarism.
"The war caused pain and suffering to the people in Japan and many Asian countries," Hashimoto said in the main government memorial ceremony for Japan's war dead.
"I solemnly accept this fact and would like to offer heartfelt condolences with deep remorse," the prime minister said.
Hashimoto's remarks were almost identical to the comments he made at last year's memorial ceremony.
Last year Hashimoto became the first prime minister from the conservative, long-ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) to express remorse to Asian war victims.
In 1993, Prime Minister Morihiro Hosokawa, when leading an anti-LDP coalition government, became the first premier to offer a clear apology in the annual August 15 ceremony.
Socialist Prime Minister Tomiichi Murayama followed suit in offering apologies at the next two war-end anniversary ceremonies.
Hashimoto said it was important to look back at the past in order to "build a permanent peace and avoid incurring the disaster and terror of war".
Following Hashimoto's comments and a moment of silent prayer, Emperor Akihito addressed the crowd at Tokyo's Nippon Budokan arena.
"Reflecting on this history, I pray from the bottom of my heart that the ravages of war will never be repeated," Akihito said.
Prior to the ceremony, seven members of Hashimoto's cabinet visited a Tokyo shrine where the souls of Japan's war dead are entombed, including war criminals.

Among those paying their respects at the controversial Shinto religious site known as the Yasukuni Shrine were Health and Welfare Minister Junichiro Koizumi and the Minister of International Trade and Industry Shinji Sato.
Hashimoto did not visit the shrine.
When he did so on July 29 last year, the visit triggered bitter criticism from China and other Asian nations that were victims of Japanese militarism.
